draft_first_round.note: Exact name+pick match between nflverse draft_picks (PFR-sourced) and Wikipedia List of Seattle Seahawks first-round draft picks. Position/college naming can differ in abbreviation, not counted as disagreement if player+pick match.
draft_first_round.interpretation: 36 exact + 3 formatting-variant matches (John L. Williams, L. J. Collier spacing, Byron Murphy II suffix) = 39/44 first-rounders matched on player+pick. Remaining 5 (Walter Jones 1997, Chris McIntosh 2000, Steve Hutchinson 2001, Earl Thomas 2010, Jaxon Smith-Njigba 2023) were not parsed from the Wikipedia table due to multi-pick-year row structure in the parser, NOT because sources disagreed; those 5 are therefore treated as single-source pending manual parse, not as disagreements. No true player/pick disagreements found.

depth_roster.method: All 69 depth-chart last names found on official seahawks.com roster page text at fetch time (69/69). This cross-checks player is on official roster, NOT depth order or injury status.

records_key_spot_checks.method: Key records in Wikipedia List of Seattle Seahawks team records compared to search-indexed reputable reporting: Russell Wilson 452 passing yards game (Field Gulls/ESPN reporting), Shaun Alexander 266 rushing game, Steve Largent 261 receiving game - all matched the records list values.
records_key_spot_checks.result: matched for spot-checked key records; full records list remains Wikipedia/PFR-cited as source 1, with most individual records NOT independently re-fetched from PFR (blocked by Cloudflare 403 on this box) - therefore labeled single-source pending in app except spot-checked items

games_h2h_playoffs.method: Computed from nflverse games file. Cross-check: 2025 season W-L 14-3 and Super Bowl LX result in Wikipedia season table matches computed regular-season record from games file (14-3). ESPN schedule endpoint was probed but its season parameter response was ambiguous, so it was NOT used as a confirming W-L count - labeled single-source (computed) pending a clean second count.

injuries.method: ESPN league injuries + ESPN roster injuries (same publisher, counts as ONE source). No independent second injury source successfully parsed (NFL.com injuries page returned 404). Therefore injuries are labeled SINGLE-SOURCE (ESPN) in app.
